```{r}
the.seed <- 42
set.seed(the.seed)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(gprofiler2)
})
```

```{r}
sample.name <- "brain_DV200"
```

## The tumour microenvironment (TME)

In glioblastoma, the main non-tumour cells are the **tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs)**. They come from two origins : **microglia** (the resident macrophages of the brain) and **bone marrow-derived macrophages (BDM)** recruited from the blood. BDM are often linked to a more immunosuppressive environment. We also look at the few T cells : glioblastoma is a "cold" tumour with few, often exhausted, T cells.

```{r}
load(paste0('../data/processed_data/', sample.name, '_STATES.rda'))

# Myeloid cells not called malignant by inferCNV
myeloid <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = celltype == "Myeloid" & cnv_status == "Normal")
ncol(myeloid)
```

`r ncol(myeloid)` myeloid cells were retained for the analysis of the TAMs.

## Origin of the TAMs : microglia or BDM ?

Microglia express P2RY12, TMEM119, CX3CR1 or SALL1, BDM and monocytes express CD163, MRC1, TGFBI, CCR2 or ITGA4 (CD49d).

```{r}
mg_genes <- c("P2RY12", "TMEM119", "CX3CR1", "SALL1", "P2RY13")
bdm_genes <- c("CD163", "MRC1", "TGFBI", "CCR2", "ITGA4", "LYZ", "FCN1")

c(mg_genes, bdm_genes)[!c(mg_genes, bdm_genes) %in% rownames(myeloid)]  # genes missing from the probe panel

myeloid <- AddModuleScore(myeloid, features = list(intersect(mg_genes, rownames(myeloid)),
                                                   intersect(bdm_genes, rownames(myeloid))),
                          name = "origin_", seed = the.seed)
myeloid$score_microglia <- myeloid$origin_1
myeloid$score_BDM <- myeloid$origin_2
myeloid$origin <- ifelse(myeloid$score_microglia > myeloid$score_BDM, "Microglia-like", "BDM-like")

table(myeloid$origin)
pct_bdm <- round(100 * mean(myeloid$origin == "BDM-like"))

ggplot(myeloid@meta.data, aes(x = score_BDM, y = score_microglia, colour = origin)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) + geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") + theme_classic()
```

**Observation**: `r pct_bdm`% of the TAMs look BDM-like and `r 100 - pct_bdm`% microglia-like. A substantial share of recruited macrophages is typical of glioblastoma. The two scores form a continuum rather than two separate groups, so the split is approximate (FCN1 is not in the probe panel).

## Sub-populations of TAMs

We re-cluster the myeloid cells alone to find sub-populations.

```{r}
myeloid <- FindVariableFeatures(myeloid, nfeatures = 2000, verbose = FALSE)
myeloid <- ScaleData(myeloid, verbose = FALSE)
myeloid <- RunPCA(myeloid, npcs = 20, verbose = FALSE)
myeloid <- FindNeighbors(myeloid, dims = 1:15, verbose = FALSE)
myeloid <- FindClusters(myeloid, resolution = 0.3, verbose = FALSE)
myeloid <- RunUMAP(myeloid, dims = 1:15, verbose = FALSE)

table(myeloid$seurat_clusters)
DimPlot(myeloid, label = TRUE) + DimPlot(myeloid, group.by = "origin")
```

Markers of origin and of function (pro-inflammatory, immunosuppressive / anti-inflammatory, antigen presentation, lipid metabolism, hypoxia) per sub-cluster

```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 4.5
tam_markers <- list(
  "Microglia"     = c("P2RY12", "TMEM119", "CX3CR1"),
  "BDM / mono"    = c("CD163", "TGFBI", "LYZ", "FCN1"),
  "Pro-infl."     = c("IL1B", "TNF", "CCL3", "CCL4", "NFKBIA"),
  "Immunosupp."   = c("MRC1", "IL10", "TGFB1", "SPP1"),
  "Antigen pres." = c("HLA-DRA", "CD74"),
  "Lipid"         = c("APOE", "APOC1", "TREM2"),
  "Hypoxia"       = c("VEGFA", "ADM", "BNIP3"),
  "Cycling"       = c("MKI67", "TOP2A"))
tam_markers <- lapply(tam_markers, intersect, rownames(myeloid))

DotPlot(myeloid, features = tam_markers) + RotatedAxis() +
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 9))
```

### Quality check of the sub-clusters

The library size, the detection of tumour genes (GFAP, SOX2) and the CNV signal were compared between the sub-clusters, to verify that none of them is driven by tumour RNA or by malignant cells.

```{r}
tam_qc <- myeloid@meta.data %>%
  mutate(GFAP = GetAssayData(myeloid, layer = "counts")["GFAP", ] > 0,
         SOX2 = GetAssayData(myeloid, layer = "counts")["SOX2", ] > 0) %>%
  group_by(subcluster = seurat_clusters) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            median_genes = median(nFeature_RNA),
            median_UMI = median(nCount_RNA),
            pct_BDM_like = round(100 * mean(origin == "BDM-like")),
            pct_GFAP = round(100 * mean(GFAP)),
            pct_SOX2 = round(100 * mean(SOX2)),
            median_chr7_minus_chr10 = round(median(chr7_minus_chr10), 3))

knitr::kable(tam_qc)

# Quantities used in the text
gfap_range <- range(tam_qc$pct_GFAP)
sox2_range <- range(tam_qc$pct_SOX2)
chr_range <- range(tam_qc$median_chr7_minus_chr10)
highest_gfap <- tam_qc$subcluster[which.max(tam_qc$pct_GFAP)]
```

GFAP, one of the most abundant transcripts of the tumour, was detected in `r gfap_range[1]` to `r gfap_range[2]`% of the cells of the sub-clusters, and SOX2 in `r sox2_range[1]` to `r sox2_range[2]`%. The median chr7 - chr10 contrast of the sub-clusters ranged from `r chr_range[1]` to `r chr_range[2]`, so they do not carry the tumour CNV signal. The tumour RNA of the sample was corrected with SoupX during the quality control. The residual detection of tumour genes in macrophages can come from remaining ambient RNA or from phagocytosed tumour material; it is highest in sub-cluster `r highest_gfap`, whose profile is interpreted with caution.

### Markers of the TAM sub-clusters

Genes over-expressed in each sub-cluster compared with the other myeloid cells were identified; they were used to name the sub-clusters and for the GO enrichment.

```{r}
tam_deg <- FindAllMarkers(myeloid, only.pos = TRUE, min.pct = 0.25,
                          logfc.threshold = 0.5, verbose = FALSE) %>%
  filter(p_val_adj < 0.05)

table(tam_deg$cluster)
tam_deg %>% group_by(cluster) %>% slice_max(avg_log2FC, n = 10) %>%
  summarise(top_genes = paste(gene, collapse = ", "))
```

### Annotation of the TAM sub-clusters

```{r}
# Assign the labels of the sub-clusters
tam_labels <- c("0" = "Microglia-like TAM",
                "1" = "SPP1+ BDM-like TAM",
                "2" = "MRC1+ BDM",
                "3" = "Hypoxic TAM")

# Stop if the labels do not cover exactly the current sub-clusters
stopifnot(setequal(names(tam_labels), levels(myeloid$seurat_clusters)))

# Audit table: size, strongest markers and assigned label of each sub-cluster
tam_audit <- tam_deg %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  slice_max(avg_log2FC, n = 4, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(top_markers = paste(gene, collapse = ", ")) %>%
  mutate(cells = as.integer(table(myeloid$seurat_clusters)[as.character(cluster)]),
         label = tam_labels[as.character(cluster)])
tam_audit

myeloid$tam_type <- unname(tam_labels[as.character(myeloid$seurat_clusters)])

DimPlot(myeloid, group.by = "tam_type", label = TRUE, repel = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Share of BDM-like cells per sub-cluster, for the text
bdm_by_sub <- setNames(tam_qc$pct_BDM_like, as.character(tam_qc$subcluster))

# Mean expression of pro-inflammatory and immunosuppressive genes in all TAMs
tam_data <- GetAssayData(myeloid, layer = "data")
proinflammatory <- intersect(c("IL1B", "TNF"), rownames(myeloid))
immunosuppressive <- intersect(c("CD163", "SPP1", "MRC1"), rownames(myeloid))
mean_proinf <- round(mean(Matrix::rowMeans(tam_data[proinflammatory, , drop = FALSE])), 2)
mean_immunosupp <- round(mean(Matrix::rowMeans(tam_data[immunosuppressive, , drop = FALSE])), 2)
```

-   **0 - Microglia-like TAM** (`r bdm_by_sub[["0"]]`% BDM-like): the markers include P2RY12, CH25H, CCL3L1 and PLD4, a microglial and activated profile.

-   **1 - SPP1+ BDM-like TAM** (`r bdm_by_sub[["1"]]`% BDM-like): the markers include SPP1, APOC2, SLC7A5 and TNFRSF11B. This label is provisional and rests on these genes.

-   **2 - MRC1+ BDM** (`r bdm_by_sub[["2"]]`% BDM-like): the markers include CLEC10A, SIGLEC1, CD209 and ALDH1A1, a monocyte-derived macrophage profile.

-   **3 - Hypoxic TAM** (`r bdm_by_sub[["3"]]`% BDM-like): the markers include ADM, TRIB3, SLC2A1, CXCL8 and PLOD2. These macrophages share the hypoxia programme of the MES-like tumour cells, and they probably live in the same hypoxic areas.

-   Overall, the mean log-normalised expression of the pro-inflammatory genes (`r paste(proinflammatory, collapse = ", ")`) was `r mean_proinf` and that of the immunosuppressive genes (`r paste(immunosuppressive, collapse = ", ")`) was `r mean_immunosupp`, which indicates `r ifelse(mean_immunosupp > mean_proinf, "a TAM population leaning towards an immunosuppressive profile, as usually described in glioblastoma", "no clear immunosuppressive profile")`.

## GO enrichment of the TAM sub-populations

Same approach as for the tumour states: the genes over-expressed in each sub-cluster (above) were used for a GO Biological Process enrichment with g:Profiler, with the genes detected in the myeloid cells as background.


```{r}
detected_myeloid <- rownames(myeloid)[Matrix::rowSums(GetAssayData(myeloid, layer = "counts") > 0) >= 10]

go_tam <- gost(query = split(tam_deg$gene, tam_deg$cluster), organism = "hsapiens", sources = "GO:BP",
               custom_bg = detected_myeloid, domain_scope = "custom",
               correction_method = "g_SCS", multi_query = FALSE)

go_tam_res <- go_tam$result
go_tam_res %>% group_by(query) %>% slice_min(p_value, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(query, term_name, p_value, intersection_size, term_size)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 9
top_go_tam <- go_tam_res %>%
  filter(term_size <= 500) %>%
  group_by(query) %>% slice_min(p_value, n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup()

ggplot(top_go_tam, aes(x = -log10(p_value), y = reorder(term_name, -log10(p_value)), size = intersection_size)) +
  geom_point(colour = "darkorange") +
  facet_wrap(~ query, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "-log10(adjusted p-value)", y = NULL, size = "Genes")
```

### Observations

```{r}
# Top specific GO terms per sub-cluster (general terms removed), for the text
top_terms_tam <- go_tam_res %>%
  filter(term_size <= 500) %>%
  group_by(query) %>%
  slice_min(p_value, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  summarise(terms = paste(term_name, collapse = "; "))
top_terms_tam <- setNames(top_terms_tam$terms, top_terms_tam$query)
```

-   **Sub-cluster 0 (microglia-like TAM)**: `r top_terms_tam[["0"]]`.

-   **Sub-cluster 1 (SPP1+ BDM-like TAM)**: `r top_terms_tam[["1"]]`.

-   **Sub-cluster 2 (MRC1+ BDM)**: `r top_terms_tam[["2"]]`.

-   **Sub-cluster 3 (hypoxic TAM)**: `r top_terms_tam[["3"]]`.

The terms were read together with the marker genes of each sub-cluster, which show a hypoxia programme in sub-cluster 3.

## T cells

Only `r sum(sobjFiltrd$celltype == "T/NK cells")` T/NK cells were annotated, so this is indicative. We look at the type (CD8 / CD4 / regulatory), cytotoxicity, and exhaustion markers (PDCD1 = PD-1, HAVCR2 = TIM-3, LAG3, TOX, CTLA4).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3
tcells <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = celltype == "T/NK cells" & cnv_status == "Normal")
ncol(tcells)

t_markers <- list(
  "Type"         = c("CD8A", "CD4", "FOXP3", "NKG7"),
  "Cytotoxic"    = c("GZMA", "GZMB", "PRF1", "IFNG"),
  "Naive/memory" = c("IL7R", "CCR7", "TCF7"),
  "Exhaustion"   = c("PDCD1", "HAVCR2", "LAG3", "TOX", "CTLA4"),
  "Cycling"      = c("MKI67"))
t_markers <- lapply(t_markers, intersect, rownames(tcells))

DotPlot(tcells, features = t_markers, group.by = "orig.ident") + RotatedAxis() +
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 9))

# % of T cells expressing each marker
t_pct <- round(100 * Matrix::rowMeans(GetAssayData(tcells, layer = "counts")[unlist(t_markers), ] > 0))
t_pct

# Number of cells expressing FOXP3
n_foxp3 <- sum(GetAssayData(tcells, layer = "counts")["FOXP3", ] > 0)
```

### Observations

These observations are indicative only (`r ncol(tcells)` cells).

-   A mix of CD8 (CD8A in `r t_pct[["CD8A"]]`% of the cells) and CD4 (`r t_pct[["CD4"]]`%) T cells, with few regulatory T cells (FOXP3 in `r t_pct[["FOXP3"]]`%, i.e. `r n_foxp3` cells).

-   Cytotoxic genes are present (GZMA `r t_pct[["GZMA"]]`%, NKG7 `r t_pct[["NKG7"]]`%, PRF1 `r t_pct[["PRF1"]]`%), IFNG is detected in `r t_pct[["IFNG"]]`% of the cells and MKI67 in `r t_pct[["MKI67"]]`%.

-   Exhaustion markers are found in a part of the cells (PD-1 `r t_pct[["PDCD1"]]`%, TIM-3 `r t_pct[["HAVCR2"]]`%, LAG3 `r t_pct[["LAG3"]]`%, CTLA4 `r t_pct[["CTLA4"]]`%, TOX `r t_pct[["TOX"]]`%).

-   Few T cells, with cytotoxic potential, little IFNG and little proliferation, together with exhaustion markers, fit the "cold", poorly active immune environment described in glioblastoma. With `r ncol(tcells)` cells this remains a hint, not a conclusion.

### Limits

-   A residual tumour signal remains in the TAMs after the SoupX correction (GFAP detected in `r gfap_range[1]` to `r gfap_range[2]`% of the cells of the sub-clusters), which can blur their profiles.

-   The origin (microglia vs BDM) is based on a few markers and forms a continuum.

-   A single tumour, and cells of one sample are not independent replicates for the GO p-values.

```{r}
save(myeloid, tcells, file = paste0('../data/processed_data/', sample.name, '_TME.rda'))
```
